title: MongoDB password with a space fails authentication: percent-encode the password in spring.mongodb.password
symptom: Authentication against MongoDB fails for an account whose password contains a space, and the value the driver receives differs from the configured password ('my+secret' instead of 'my secret').
cause: The MongoDB driver builds its credentials from a connection string, in which reserved and special characters must be percent-encoded, and it does not decode the password again when it comes from separate properties, so a raw space is mangled.
fixSummary: Percent-encode the password yourself in the properties file: spring.mongodb.password=my%20secret. The driver then receives an unambiguous connection string and reads the space correctly; keep username, host, database and authentication-database as they are.
